# Study flashcards

Flashcards in five boxes: study what is due today, a card at a time, and the ones you miss come back first.

**Read docs/ first.** It's this app's memory: what it's for, the shape of its data, the decisions made and why, and what's missing. Keep it current whenever you change the app.

## Screens
- Study (src/screens/study.tsx): how many cards are due, topic pills, Study now, and the cards per box. Studying is on the same screen: the question, Show answer, then Didn't know or Knew it.
- Cards (src/screens/cards.tsx): every card by topic with its box; add, edit or delete one (with Undo).

The data and the box rules are in src/lib/cards.ts; the shared pieces (sections, rows, bar, sheet, pills) in src/components/kit.tsx.

## Tests
`npm test` runs Vitest. Tests live in tests/*.test.tsx and use Testing Library (render, screen, userEvent) with the jest-dom matchers; `amber` (from "amber") shows what was saved. A test can start over a sample of the app's data, so each test here sets the data it needs first (beforeEach). Pinto Notes runs them, and a quick check that the app opens and its buttons work, on every save: a version that fails isn't shown to the person; the last one that passed keeps running until the failures are fixed.

**Every feature you add gets a test like the ones in tests/app.test.tsx**: do what the person does, check what they see, and check what was saved. When the app changes on purpose, change its tests to match the new behaviour. Never weaken, skip or delete a test just to make it pass: fix the app instead.

## How this app runs in Pinto Notes

- It is the note: opening the note opens the app, on iPhone (320-440 pt wide, safe areas, the keyboard shrinks the view) and on the Mac (a window from about 500 to 1,800 px, resized live). Light and dark follow the device.
- A normal Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui project. Pinto Notes compiles it when a file is saved (TSX, the @/ alias, imports without extensions, Tailwind from the classes used) and says what broke; nothing is installed. React runs on preact/compat.
- Available by name: react, react-dom, radix-ui, lucide-react, recharts, date-fns, zod, motion, sonner, react-day-picker, clsx, tailwind-merge, class-variance-authority, amber-router (Router, Route, route(), back()), chart.js, d3, three, tone, dayjs, marked, dompurify, animejs, canvas-confetti.
- Data is JSON that Pinto Notes keeps for the app (encrypted, synced, with Undo): useStore(key, initial), useCollection(name), useSettings(defaults), batch(fn), setSummary(text) from "@/lib/amber". localStorage works too and is kept the same way. The person's AI reads and edits it as data.json, so keep its shape simple and describe it in docs/README.md.
- No network except hosts the person allows: declare them in index.html with <meta name="amber-needs" content='{"hosts": ["api.open-meteo.com"]}'> and call fetch(url) from "@/lib/amber"; API keys live in Pinto Notes › Settings › API Keys (declare { "keys": [{ "name", "hosts", "query" or "header" }] } and pass { key: name }).
- The device: device.openURL(url) opens a link once the person agrees to it, share(file) exports one, device.photos.pick() and device.files.pick() let the person choose. Reminders, Calendar, notifications, the camera, contacts, location, Maps and on-device AI are not available yet.

# Study flashcards: notes for whoever works on this app next

## What it's for
A student studies flashcards a few minutes a day, mostly on their iPhone. Their AI makes the cards from pasted lecture notes or a chapter, and can quiz them in chat too, moving cards between boxes the same way the app does.

## Data
data.json, all under "values" (the person's AI reads and edits it directly):
- cards: [{ id, q, a, topic, box, seen }]
  - q and a are the question and the answer, short and plain.
  - box is 1 to 5 (Leitner boxes). New cards start in box 1 with no seen.
  - seen is the day the card was last studied ("yyyy-mm-dd").
- A card is due when it has no seen, or when seen plus its box's gap has come: box 1 after 1 day, 2 after 2, 3 after 4, 4 after 8, 5 after 16 (GAP in src/lib/cards.ts).
- Grading: knew it moves the card up one box (at most 5); didn't know puts it back in box 1. Both set seen to today. An AI quizzing in chat should do the same.
- ids are any unique text ("c21").

## Decisions
- The first screen says how many cards are due and has one big button, Study now. Topic pills narrow it to one subject.
- A session asks the lowest box first, one card at a time: the question, Show answer, then Didn't know or Knew it. The answer fades in; there is no 3D flip.
- The person is in control without the AI: add, edit (tap a card) and delete cards; deleting shows Undo in a bar at the top of the screen.
- The Boxes chart shows where the cards are, so progress is visible without a streak.
- The app sets the note's summary line to "12 cards due today".

## Known gaps
- No typed answers or multiple choice; grading is the person's own call.
- No images on cards (files could be added with device.photos.pick()).

import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from "vitest"
import { render, screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { amber } from "amber"
import { route } from "amber-router"
import App from "@/App"
import { iso } from "@/lib/cards"

// Each test does what the person does, then checks what they see and what was saved in data.json.
const values = () => amber.data.values ?? {}
const today = iso(new Date())
const go = async (name: string) => userEvent.click((await screen.findAllByRole("link", { name }))[0])
const card = (id: string, q: string, a: string, topic: string, box = 1, seen?: string) => ({ id, q, a, topic, box, ...(seen ? { seen } : {}) })

// Start each test from no cards, whatever data the app holds.
beforeEach(async () => {
  route("/")
  await amber.store.set("cards", [])
})

describe("Study", () => {
  it("studies the due cards: shows the answer, then moves each card by how you did", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("cards", [
      card("c1", "Where does glycolysis happen?", "In the cytoplasm", "Biology", 2),
      card("c2", "What is ATP for?", "Energy the cell can use", "Biology", 1),
    ])
    render(<App />)
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("due")).toHaveTextContent("2 cards")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Study now" }))
    // Lowest box first.
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("question")).toHaveTextContent("What is ATP for?")
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("answer")).toBeNull()
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Show answer" }))
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("answer")).toHaveTextContent("Energy the cell can use")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Knew it" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().cards[1]).toEqual(card("c2", "What is ATP for?", "Energy the cell can use", "Biology", 2, today)))

    expect(await screen.findByTestId("question")).toHaveTextContent("Where does glycolysis happen?")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Show answer" }))
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Didn't know" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().cards[0]).toEqual(card("c1", "Where does glycolysis happen?", "In the cytoplasm", "Biology", 1, today)))

    expect(await screen.findByText("1 knew, 1 to see again")).toBeInTheDocument()
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Done" }))
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("due")).toHaveTextContent("Nothing due")
  })

  it("leaves out cards that aren't due yet", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("cards", [card("c1", "Q one", "A one", "Biology", 3, today), card("c2", "Q two", "A two", "Biology", 1)])
    render(<App />)
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("due")).toHaveTextContent("1 card")
    expect(screen.getByText("2 cards in 1 topic")).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("studies one topic", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("cards", [card("c1", "Q bio", "A", "Biology"), card("c2", "Q chem", "A", "Chemistry"), card("c3", "Q chem 2", "A", "Chemistry")])
    render(<App />)
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("due")).toHaveTextContent("3 cards")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("radio", { name: "Chemistry" }))
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("due")).toHaveTextContent("2 cards")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Study now" }))
    expect(await screen.findByText("1 of 2")).toBeInTheDocument()
    expect(screen.getByTestId("question")).toHaveTextContent("Q chem")
  })

  it("ends a session early", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("cards", [card("c1", "Q one", "A one", "Biology")])
    render(<App />)
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Study now" }))
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "End" }))
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("due")).toHaveTextContent("1 card")
    expect(values().cards[0].seen).toBeUndefined()
  })
})

describe("Cards", () => {
  it("adds a card to box 1, due at once", async () => {
    render(<App />)
    await go("Cards")
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Add" }))
    await userEvent.type(await screen.findByLabelText("Question"), "What is a codon?")
    await userEvent.type(screen.getByLabelText("Answer"), "Three bases")
    await userEvent.type(screen.getByLabelText("Topic"), "DNA")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Add card" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().cards.map(({ id, ...c }: { id: string }) => c)).toEqual([{ q: "What is a codon?", a: "Three bases", topic: "DNA", box: 1 }]))
    expect(await screen.findByText("What is a codon?")).toBeInTheDocument()
    await go("Study")
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("due")).toHaveTextContent("1 card")
  })

  it("edits a card", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("cards", [card("c1", "Q one", "A one", "Biology", 3, today)])
    route("/cards")
    render(<App />)
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Edit Q one" }))
    const answer = await screen.findByLabelText("Answer")
    expect(answer).toHaveValue("A one")
    await userEvent.clear(answer)
    await userEvent.type(answer, "A better answer")
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Save" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().cards).toEqual([card("c1", "Q one", "A better answer", "Biology", 3, today)]))
    expect(await screen.findByText("A better answer")).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("says how to start when there are no cards", async () => {
    render(<App />)
    expect(await screen.findByText("No cards yet. Add the first one in the Cards tab.")).toBeInTheDocument()
    await go("Cards")
    expect(await screen.findByText(/^No cards yet\. Tap Add/)).toBeInTheDocument()
  })

  it("deletes a card, with Undo", async () => {
    await amber.store.set("cards", [card("c1", "Q one", "A one", "Biology"), card("c2", "Q two", "A two", "Biology")])
    route("/cards")
    render(<App />)
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Delete Q one" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().cards.map((c: { id: string }) => c.id)).toEqual(["c2"]))
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByText("Q one")).not.toBeInTheDocument())
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Undo" }))
    await waitFor(() => expect(values().cards.map((c: { id: string }) => c.id)).toEqual(["c1", "c2"]))
  })
})
